title: Professional Email Terms: Subscriptions and Email Domains
content:
**Clause 1. Several subscriptions, one per email domain.** A customer may hold several Professional Email subscriptions, one per email domain. A new subscription may be ordered for an email domain only when no other subscription for that domain is in status provisioning, active, suspended, cancel pending or expired.

**Clause 2. No count limit per customer.** The number of Professional Email subscriptions one customer may hold is not capped; the only limit is one live subscription per email domain.

**Clause 3. What decides it.** The judgement rests on the subscription records, not on the customer's statement: the email domain of each existing subscription, as recorded in lowercase and verbatim, is compared with the email domain of the new order, and the status of each matching subscription is read.

## Status of an existing subscription for the same domain

| Status of the other subscription for that domain | New order for the domain |
|---|---|
| provisioning | not allowed |
| active | not allowed |
| suspended | not allowed |
| cancel pending | not allowed |
| expired | not allowed |
| cancelled, or no other subscription for the domain | allowed |

## Examples (hypothetical domains)

- A customer holding a subscription for `northfield-tiles.example` in status active orders a second subscription for `northfield-tiles.example`: not allowed.
- The same customer orders a subscription for `harbour-kayaks.example`, for which no subscription exists: allowed, and the customer then holds two subscriptions.
- A subscription for `harbour-kayaks.example` that is cancelled does not stand in the way of a new order for that domain.
